camps.name: Holden Pass and the slab bivies above
camps.why: Sleeping at the saddle puts the West Ridge gullies right above camp, so the loose summit day starts early and short; water is nearby and sites are established.

camps.name: Holden Lake
camps.why: The Bonanza base camp, lower and buggier, with a longer summit day for Martin; use it when you also want Bonanza or arrive too late to carry on to the pass.

camps.name: Holden Village
camps.why: Indoor beds and meals at 3,200 ft the night before or after the trip; it fits a ferry schedule but adds a full climbing day of distance if you sleep there on the way in.

camps.name: Holden Ballpark Campground
camps.why: A cheap open field about a mile above the village for a night before or after; exposed, with few sites, and too low to help the summit day.

plan_conflict: Holden Lake is filed as a main camp, but this plan and most parties sleep both nights at Holden Pass.

camps.name: Massie Lake basin
camps.why: The only practical camp for the peak: lake water, a toilet and flat sites, with the summit scramble a short half day above.

camps.name: Trinity trailhead roadhead
camps.why: A staging spot after the long gravel drive; sleeping here only saves an hour of driving and adds to the next day's carry.

camps.name: The Chiwawa River trail camps above the bridge
camps.why: Flat, sheltered and on the river; a fallback for a late start or the walk out, but it leaves a steep climb to the lake the next morning.

camps.name: The benches above Massie Lake — no established camp
camps.why: A cold dry bivy only for a crest start at first light; you carry water up and gain little, since the peak is a short day from the lake.

camps.name: Leroy Basin
camps.why: The standard base for Fernow: a meadow at about 6,100 ft with water, reached by the steep climbers' path, and it cuts the summit day to the shortest possible.

camps.name: Swamp Creek Camp — the base for Needle Peak, Mount Lyall and Lyall Ridge
camps.why: The working base for Lyall on the Crest trail corridor; sleeping here shortens the summit day, and the unmaintained trail beyond is brushy with no better site.

camps.name: Purple Point and Harlequin — the landing camps, and the boat that decides the trip
camps.why: The night before the walk if the boat times badly; it is far down the valley, so you start with a long shuttle and walk.

camps.name: High Bridge Camp — the shuttle terminus and the base for McGregor Mountain
camps.why: The first camp past the bus; good for a late arrival, but it adds about eight miles to the approach and makes day one much longer.

camps.name: Fivemile Camp, Agnes Creek
camps.why: A comfortable halfway camp on the trail; stopping here splits the approach but leaves roughly three miles more to Swamp Creek the next morning.

camps.name: Leroy Basin
camps.why: The lower, easier camp on the standard Maude approach; it adds a long day over the cols to reach the glacier, so this route's parties go higher to the Ice Lakes.

camps.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds
camps.why: Staging camps at the end of a long rough drive; they save nothing on the climb but spare a tired late-night drive.

new_camps.name: Ice Lakes bivy
new_camps.why: Bivy ledges beside the Ice Lakes near the South Ridge; they sit within reach of the glacier crossing and icefall, and the same ledges are used on the descent.
new_camps.water: Lake water at the Ice Lakes below.
new_camps.capacity: A few small flat ledges; space is limited.
new_camps.permit: Glacier Peak Wilderness permit required; check current rules.
new_camps.notes: Reached by about 4,000 ft of gain from the trailhead. After the summit the party drops back to these ledges for the second night before hiking out.

plan_conflict: Leroy Basin is filed as the main camp, but this plan sleeps at a bivy above the Ice Lakes both nights.

camps.name: Leroy Basin
camps.why: The climbers' basin for Maude from the west: meadow sites with water at about 6,100 ft, and the Nothing Couloir loop starts within a short walk.

camps.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds
camps.why: Staging camps after the rough gravel drive; sleeping here helps a late arrival but adds the whole approach to the first day.

camps.name: Lyman Lakes and Cloudy Pass
camps.why: Past Spider Gap on day one; the lakes and pass have many sites and water, and North Star is an easy day from the pass trail.

camps.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds
camps.why: Staging camps at the road end; useful the night before an early start for the long Spider Gap day.

camps.name: Spider Meadow and Phelps Basin
camps.why: The usual first night for a four-day version: it splits the gap crossing in half, but adds a day and a second carry over the snow.

camps.name: Holden Village
camps.why: Indoor beds if you come in from the Railroad Creek side; not on this over-the-gap plan, and the road end is a day's walk away.

camps.name: Holden Ballpark Campground
camps.why: A cheap tent field above the village for the Railroad Creek approach; exposed with few sites and not used on the Spider Gap plan.

camps.name: Lower Lyman Lake
camps.why: The base for this Holden-side plan: eight miles up Railroad Creek, with lake water and sites, and the south flank starts straight from camp.

camps.name: Lyman Lakes and Cloudy Pass
camps.why: The higher group of sites a mile or two on; it gives a shorter walk to the pass trail but adds carrying and exposure to wind.

camps.name: Holden Village
camps.why: Indoor beds the night before the trip if the boat times badly; it costs lodging fees and adds eight miles to the first day.

camps.name: Holden Ballpark Campground
camps.why: A cheap tent field above the village for a night before the walk in; exposed with few sites and not used on a normal two-night plan.

camps.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds
camps.why: Camps on the far side of Spider Gap for the other approach; not slept at on this boat-and-bus plan.

camps.name: Spider Meadow and Phelps Basin
camps.why: The first night for the over-the-gap approach from Phelps Creek; not used when you come in from Holden.

camps.name: Rebel Camp
camps.why: A trailside camp about five miles up Railroad Creek; a split option for a slow party, but it leaves a longer second leg to the lake.

plan_conflict: Lyman Lakes and Cloudy Pass is filed as a second main camp, but this plan sleeps at Lower Lyman Lake.

camps.name: Leroy Basin
camps.why: The standard camp for the Jack: meadow sites with water at about 6,100 ft, about three hours below the summit on loose scree.

camps.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds
camps.why: Staging camps at the end of the rough road for a late arrival; they leave the full approach and the summit for one long day.

camps.name: Leroy Basin camp
camps.why: The only practical high camp on this approach: meadow sites and water at about 6,100 ft, giving a long but possible summit day over two passes.

camps.name: Louis Creek Basin camp
camps.why: A basin camp right under the southwest slopes, so the summit is a short half day; it costs a long first day over the High Pass route.

camps.name: Buck Creek Pass and the High Pass camps
camps.why: Good established sites with water, and a shorter first day; the next morning's walk and the dry ridge crossing to the basin add a few hours.

plan_conflict: Buck Creek Pass and the High Pass camps is filed as the main camp, but this plan carries on to Louis Creek Basin both nights.

camps.name: Butterfly Butte and the Pilz Glacier basin camps
camps.why: The climbing camp for Chalangin and Luahna: benches near Butterfly Butte with water, and the Pilz Glacier approach starts nearby.

camps.name: Napeequa Valley floor near Louis Creek
camps.why: A lower, warmer camp by the river after the pass; it shortens the first day but adds roughly a thousand feet and a longer summit day.

plan_conflict: The plan puts camp at about 6,200 ft while the camp on file sits near 5,850 ft; the exact bench was not confirmed.

new_camps.name: Chalangin Basin high camp
new_camps.why: The only high camp on the Thunder Creek approach; it puts the snowy southwest face right above you and saves a long bushwhack on the summit day.
new_camps.water: Thunder Creek and snowmelt in the basin; not confirmed.
new_camps.capacity: Unknown; expect a few small sites.
new_camps.permit: Wilderness permit required; check current rules.
new_camps.notes: Reached by leaving the White River trail and bushwhacking up Thunder Creek through alder and burned blowdown. Camp location comes from the trip plan and was not confirmed independently.

camps.name: Boulder Basin camp
camps.why: A basin camp at about 5,000 to 5,300 ft below Boulder Pass; water and a south view of Clark, with the glacier reached in an alpine start.

camps.name: Boulder Pass and Thunder Basin, White River
camps.why: A higher camp near the pass; it shortens the summit day but adds carry and a colder, more exposed night.

plan_conflict: Boulder Pass and Thunder Basin is also filed as main, but this plan sleeps in Boulder Basin.

camps.name: Buck Creek Pass and the High Pass camps
camps.why: Established sites with water at Buck Creek Pass or Pass No Pass; Helmet Butte is a one to two hour scramble from camp.

plan_conflict: The plan's night 2 is optional; most parties summit on day 2 and hike out, so only night 1 is a normal camp.

camps.name: Boulder Creek ford camp
camps.why: A forest camp at the Boulder Creek ford after a short first day; it keeps the upper basin move for the morning with water at hand.

camps.name: Upper Boulder Basin high camp
camps.why: The high camp at about 5,700 ft, which puts Point 7970 and the glacier within reach, so the summit day is the shortest.

camps.name: Boulder Pass and Thunder Basin, White River
camps.why: A higher alternative near the pass; it saves little for Luahna and adds distance and exposure beyond the basin camp.

plan_conflict: Boulder Pass and Thunder Basin is filed as the main camp, but this plan sleeps at the Boulder Creek ford and then in upper Boulder Basin.

camps.name: Boulder Pass and Thunder Basin, White River
camps.why: A higher camp near the pass; it is farther than the basin camp and not used on this overnight plan.

new_camps.name: Boulder Creek ford camp
new_camps.why: The one night camp on this plan, at the Boulder Creek ford; it is a short walk from the cars and keeps the long climb for the morning.
new_camps.permit: Wilderness permit required; check current rules.
new_camps.notes: About four miles up the White River trail then to the ford. The plan then climbs to a high camp and out all on day 2, which is very long.

plan_conflict: The plan fits two camps (ford camp, then upper Boulder Basin) and the summit and hike out into only one night and two days; it is not workable as written.
